source.title: What Is a Cognitive Map? Organizing Knowledge for Flexible Behavior.

confidence_rationale: Authoritative review arguing explicitly that map-like coding observed in spatial tasks is an instance of a general knowledge-organising mechanism that applies across domains -- the domain-general arm of Q-083's fork, stated as the paper's thesis. Confidence is held in the moderate band because it is a review advancing a position rather than a decisive test, and because the non-spatial domains it draws on (conceptual, social, task-space) are a narrower and more structurally homogeneous set than Q-083's six.
failure_signatures: The evidence for cross-domain map-like coding is strongest where the non-spatial domain has an obvious low-dimensional metric structure (continuous concept spaces, social hierarchies); domains without such structure are not shown to be organised this way, so the generality claim is untested exactly where Q-083 is least confident.

Demonstrating that the same REPRESENTATIONAL FORMAT appears in several domains does not demonstrate that one apprehension PROCESS built all of them -- shared format is compatible with parallel domain-specific learners converging on the same code.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Map-like neural representations observed during spatial navigation are an instance of general coding mechanisms capable of organising knowledge of all kinds; the same principles for learning and deploying abstract generalisable structure appear in non-spatial conceptual, social, and task domains, and artificial agents given these principles learn brain-like map representations.
mapping.ree_translation: This is direct argumentative support for Q-083's domain-general arm: one structure-learning mechanism that inherits its content from whatever inputs it is given, rather than a family of per-domain apprehenders. Mapped to REE, it says the hippocampal-style relational machinery already in V3 is the right place to look for a domain-general apprehender, and that the domain-agnosticism Q-083 registers as untested is at least biologically plausible rather than merely convenient.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The paper argues a position; it is a review, and the cross-domain evidence it assembles is concentrated in domains that already have metric or ordinal structure resembling space (continuous concept spaces, dominance hierarchies, structured task spaces). Q-083's hardest cases -- ethical and social regularity apprehension without an obvious metric -- are precisely where this evidence thins. There is also a format-versus-process conflation risk: shared representational format across domains is weaker evidence than shared apprehension process, and REE's question is about the process.
mapping.source_context: Human and rodent electrophysiology and fMRI, plus artificial-agent modelling; review synthesising spatial and non-spatial cognitive-map findings.

confidence_components.notes: High source quality (Neuron review by the group that subsequently built TEM). Mapping fidelity is moderate: the paper supports domain-generality of the representational FORMAT more strongly than of the apprehension PROCESS, and Q-083 asks about the latter. Weighted toward mapping fidelity as an architectural claim.
